Psychosis

rule out a cause, then time itHow long, and only during mood episodes?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Likely harm to self or others, or unable to meet basic needs hospitalize first
  • Toxicology chemistry and glucose TSH then time it: brief under 1 month, schizophreniform 1 to under 6 months, schizophrenia 6 months or more
  • Delusions only, 1 month or more, Criterion A never met delusional disorder; psychosis only inside mood episodes mood disorder
What it is

Delusions, hallucinations or disorganized speech, named by how long they last and how they sit with mood episodes

Driver

Schizophrenia: genes explain about 80% of the risk in twin and family studies

Triggers

Family history non-modifiable heavy cannabis use (6 times the risk in one study)

A marked stressor, or onset during pregnancy or within 4 weeks postpartum (brief psychotic disorder)

Isolation, deafness, low vision (delusions) older age non-modifiable

Chain

Schizophrenia: prodrome active psychosis, 1 month or more (less if treated) residual; 6 months in all

Schizophreniform may evolve into schizophrenia, bipolar or schizoaffective disorder

Insights

Symptoms outlast a window re-time the whole illness

Criterion A with a mood episode psychosis 2 weeks or more without one mood most of the illness schizoaffective

Course and specifiersdetail behind the chain
Brief psychotic1 day to under 1 month, then full return to baseline; specifiers: with marked stressor; with postpartum onset (during pregnancy or within 4 weeks postpartum)
Schizophrenia6 months or more, with functional decline; onset early 20s in men, later in women
2Urgent risks
DangerLikely harm to self or others, or cannot meet basic needs
APA positionA mental disorder; hospital care can help; the patient is unable or unwilling to consent; the least restrictive option. Commitment law varies by state.

If harm is likely or basic needs go unmet, choose hospitalization first, whatever the duration; involuntarily only when the criteria and state law allow.

MedicalPsychosis with disturbed attention and awareness that develops over hours to days and fluctuates

If it occurs only during a delirium, choose the delirium workup, not a psychotic disorder.

3Differential
Look-alikes, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
SchizophreniaCriterion A with functional decline6 months or more, at least 1 month active
Delusional disorder1 or more delusions; hallucinations, if any, not prominent and tied to the delusion; works normally otherwise1 month or more; Criterion A never met: no second Criterion A symptom
Brief psychotic disorder1 or more core symptoms, often after a stressor1 day to under 1 month; full return to baseline
Schizophreniform disorderCriterion A1 to under 6 months; functional decline not required
Schizoaffective disorderCriterion A with major mood episodes at the same timePsychosis 2 weeks or more without a mood episode; mood most of the illness
Bipolar type includes a manic episode; depressive type, only major depressive episodes
Delusions with euphoric mood and less sleepMania 1 week or more (any length if hospitalized); psychosis only inside mood episodes
Delusions or hallucinations tied to a drugDuring or soon after use; lasting about 1 month after stopping suggests an independent disorder
Distress after a stressorWithin 3 months of the stressor; psychosis would be atypical
Symptoms after an event1 month or more; trauma that threatens death or injury; intrusions and avoidance
Trauma symptoms soon after the eventWithin the first month after a trauma
Psychosis with major depressive episodesPsychosis only inside the depressive episodes
Suspicious, distrustful, hypervigilantLifelong; no persistent delusion or hallucination
Psychosis from a metabolic or thyroid illness, such as hypothyroidismAbnormal chemistry, glucose or TSH, with psychosis timed to it
Inattention and reduced awareness, fluctuatingHours to days; psychosis only during the delirium
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
Symptoms past 1 monthNo longer brief psychotic disorderRe-time it: schizophreniform if Criterion A; delusions only, delusional disorder
A delusion for 1 month or more, works normally, no other Criterion A symptomDelusional disorderNot schizophrenia: Criterion A needs 2 symptoms
Psychosis after a stressor, no intrusions or avoidanceA stressor, not traumaUnder 1 month: brief psychotic disorder, not PTSD
Drank the night it began; it outlasted the drinkingSubstance cause unlikelyOne night of drinking; alcohol rarely causes psychosis directly: keep timing it
Began during stimulant intoxicationSubstance-inducedStop the drug; reassess the timing
Loss of interest with psychosis, but no depressed moodNot a major depressive episode for schizoaffective disorderCount only episodes with depressed mood

Pause point. The bait: one fixed delusion for months offered as schizophrenia (it needs a second Criterion A symptom), or a week of psychosis after a stressor offered as delusional disorder or PTSD (a week with full recovery is brief psychotic disorder).

5Diagnostic criteria
Defining criteria: schizophrenia Symptoms – 2 or more of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized or catatonic behavior, negative symptoms · Core – at least 1 is delusions, hallucinations or disorganized speech · Duration – 6 months or more in all, with at least 1 month of active symptoms (less if treated) · Decline – work or relationships fall since onset · Cause – not a substance, medication or medical condition; schizoaffective and psychotic mood disorders excluded
7Treatment
1

1st lineschizophrenia spectrum

An antipsychotic at a therapeutic dose

Full effect can take 4 to 6 weeks or more. StatPearlsAntipsychotics, especially second-generation, are first line (brief psychotic disorder source).

2

Switchstill ill after an adequate trial at a therapeutic dose

A different antipsychotic

A long-acting injectable for nonadherence or by preference.

3

Resistant2 or more adequate trials fail, adherence documented

Clozapine, with ANC (absolute neutrophil count) monitoring

One failed antipsychotic is not resistance.

First treatment by situation
SituationChooseWatch for
Brief psychotic disorderSupervision; a short antipsychotic course may be requiredPast 1 month it is no longer brief: re-time it (schizophreniform only if Criterion A)
Schizophreniform disorderAn antipsychotic plus supportive psychosocial care
Schizophrenia, first episodeAn antipsychoticSuicide risk 5% to 10% over a lifetime
Delusional disorderPsychotherapy that builds trust plus a 6-week antipsychotic trialDo not accept the delusion as real: it distorts the patient's reality and breeds distrust
Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (manic episode part of the illness)A second-generation antipsychotic, which may be enough aloneIf not enough, adding lithium, carbamazepine or valproate may help
Schizoaffective disorder, depressive typeA second-generation antipsychotic firstAdd an antidepressant if the depression needs treatment; SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors) preferred for safety
8Follow-up
Follow-up decisions
WhenDo
Judging a trialNo minimal gain by 2 weeks at a therapeutic dose predicts little later gain
Brief psychotic disorder in remissionContinue the antipsychotic 1 to 3 months (suggested)
Schizophreniform disorder resolvedContinue 12 months or longer, then taper slowly with close watch
Schizophrenia after a first episodeContinue at least 1 to 2 years; many years after a longer illness
On clozapineANC before starting, weekly for 6 months, every 2 weeks to month 12, then monthly
Stable schizophrenia, longer termFamily interventions when the family is in ongoing contact (suggested), alongside the antipsychotic
Practice
  1. 24-year-old man, previously well; for 3 months he has: believed neighbors implanted a tracker in his tooth heard voices commenting on everything he does stopped attending classes No episodes of depressed or elevated mood Urine toxicology negative · flat affect → Schizophreniform disorder → a delusion plus prominent voices for at least 1 month and under 6 months
  2. 26-year-old man; for 9 months he has: heard voices believed television hosts send him coded messages lost his job, rarely speaks, stopped bathing No episodes of depressed or elevated mood Vital signs normal · urine toxicology negative · flat affect → Schizophrenia → Criterion A symptoms with functional decline for 6 months or more
  3. 41-year-old man at a clinic visit hears voices, feels watched mood normal for 2 months manic and depressive episodes most of the past 15 years, each with voices and a persecutory belief urine toxicology negative · T 36.7 °C → Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type → voices and a persecutory belief during manic and depressive episodes, voices 2 weeks or more with a normal mood, and mood episodes over most of the illness are schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type; in bipolar I disorder the psychosis occurs only during mood episodes, and in schizophrenia mood episodes fill only a small part of the illness
  4. 46-year-old woman; for 4 months she has: written daily letters to a news anchor she has never met been certain he loves her Works full time and runs her household; no hallucinations; mood normal Vital signs normal · laboratory studies normal → Delusional disorder → an erotomanic delusion for at least 1 month, with functioning intact and no other psychotic or mood symptoms
  5. 34-year-old woman with 1 year of insulting voices and belief coworkers are poisoning her two depressive episodes (4 and 3 months): low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, guilt, poor focus voices and belief persist 4 weeks after mood normalized Toxicology negative · euthymic → Schizoaffective disorder → Criterion A concurrent with major depressive episodes, 2 weeks or more of delusions and voices without a mood episode, and mood episodes for most of the illness
  6. 29-year-old man with 1 week of euphoria: 2-hour nights, rapid talk, his savings spent believing God chose him to rule the world Similar week 2 years ago; beliefs stopped when mood settled; none between episodes Vital signs normal · toxicology negative → Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features → the psychosis occurs only during the manic episode
  7. 22-year-old man with 2 days of believing federal agents are following him smoked methamphetamine daily for 3 days barely slept No psychiatric history HR 96/min · BP 128/80 mm Hg · oriented to person, place and time → Substance-induced psychotic disorder → the delusion began during stimulant intoxication; timing ties it to the drug
  8. 27-year-old woman, 6 days after escaping a house fire sure neighbors set it to kill her; hears them whispering no nightmares, flashbacks or avoidance; no drug use; fully well 10 days later urine toxicology negative · T 36.8 °C → Brief psychotic disorder → delusions and hallucinations after a marked stressor, with full return to baseline within a month, are brief psychotic disorder; acute stress disorder brings intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance and arousal, and she has no flashbacks, nightmares or avoidance; delusional disorder needs a delusion for 1 month or more
  9. 31-year-old woman with 5 days of: believing the government hacked her phone hearing whispers at night No psychiatric history; neurologic examination normal T 37.0 C · HR 88/min · chemistry panel and TSH normal → Urine toxicology screen → the first-line test still missing after chemistry and TSH; a negative screen lowers suspicion of a drug cause; imaging needs a neurologic finding or history; lumbar puncture needs fever, meningismus or delirium
  10. 40-year-old man with 10 days of believing his coworkers are poisoning his food yesterday he bought a knife to confront them No psychiatric history Vital signs normal · urine toxicology negative · oriented to person, place and time → Hospitalization and an antipsychotic → likely harm to others: admit first, whatever the duration; involuntarily if he refuses and no less restrictive option is safe
  11. 33-year-old man treated for schizophrenia for 6 years still hears voices daily after adequate trials of risperidone, then olanzapine adherence confirmed by pill counts No suicidal or homicidal ideation Vital signs normal · flat affect → Clozapine → 2 or more failed adequate trials with documented adherence define treatment resistance
  12. 35-year-old man with 5 years of recurring major depressive episodes each episode brings voices and persecutory beliefs voices persisted 3 weeks after his mood recovered depressed for most of those 5 years; never manic Afebrile · urine toxicology negative → Schizoaffective disorder, depressive type → Criterion A with major depressive episodes, voices 2 weeks or more without one, and depression for most of the illness; never manic, so depressive type
  13. 41-year-old woman newly diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type hears voices and has felt hopeless for 2 months; denies suicidal ideation no history of manic episodes BP 118/76 mm Hg · urine toxicology negative → Second-generation antipsychotic plus an SSRI → depressive type: an antipsychotic treats the psychosis, and an SSRI may be added for the depression; a mood stabilizer such as lithium is for bipolar type
How NBME framed it: question 1

52-year-old man brought by police for strange behavior after an arrest for disturbing his neighbors for 6 months: aggressively handing out leaflets for the New Age healing business he runs from home claims special abilities to cure all physical and mental ailments very upset; sure the police and the physician are plotting against him and his business “I really have special powers; I can heal everyone in the waiting room” Denies past psychiatric problems, depression, elevated mood or hearing voices; sleeps 6 to 8 hours Examination normal · laboratory studies normal

Most likely diagnosis?

Competing answers
  • Bipolar disorder: grandiose claims; but no low or high mood, and normal sleep.
  • Brief psychotic disorder: an acute presentation after an arrest; but it lasts under 1 month, and his delusion has lasted 6.
  • Schizoaffective disorder: a persecutory delusion; but no mood episode and no second Criterion A symptom.
  • Schizophrenia: a fixed persecutory delusion; but it needs a second Criterion A symptom, and delusions are his only symptom.

Down to two: delusional disorder or schizophrenia. Delusional disorder: delusions alone (grandiose and persecutory) for 6 months; no voices, mood episode or disorganization; sleep and labs normal. (NBME says no hallucinations at all; current criteria allow minor ones tied to the delusion.)

How NBME framed it: question 2

37-year-old man with odd experiences that began 2 weeks ago, after he was fired instead of promoted a guard watched him clear his desk and walked him out six drinks at a bar over 4 hours; felt the patrons knew, were watching and talking about him next morning still felt it; closed the curtains; believed television hosts mocked him over that week a man’s voice called him a failure who would amount to nothing; went out only for food, in dark glasses to avoid recognition everything resolved by the end of the week No serious illness or medications; 2 to 3 beers nightly; marijuana once a month Examination normal · no hallucinations now · logical, goal-directed thinking · alert and oriented to person, place and time

Most likely diagnosis?

Competing answers
  • Adjustment disorder: a clear stressor; but psychotic symptoms would be atypical.
  • Delusional disorder: paranoid beliefs; but it needs 1 month or more, and his lasted a week.
  • Posttraumatic stress disorder: a distressing event; but job loss is not life-threatening, and it needs intrusions and over 1 month.
  • Schizophreniform disorder: delusions and a voice; but it needs 1 to 6 months.
  • Substance-induced psychotic disorder: six drinks and monthly cannabis; but alcohol rarely causes psychosis directly, and his cannabis use is occasional.

Down to two: brief psychotic disorder or delusional disorder. Brief psychotic disorder: paranoid delusions and a voice after a stressor, gone within a week, well under 1 month.

Pairs with Bipolar disorder: psychosis only during mania? Delirium: psychosis with a clouded, fluctuating sensorium?
Transferable rule

Rule out a cause, then ask how long the psychosis has lasted and whether it occurs only during mood episodes.
